card: This pull request adds a bip152hb network permission flag that operators can assign to peers using -whitelist or -whitebind. Bitcoin Core dynamically selects up to three high-bandwidth BIP152 compact block peers based on block arrival, which prevents operators from leveraging known low-latency topology or cross-datacenter links across reconnects. Configured peers are requested to use high-bandwidth mode immediately on handshake and do not consume any of the three automatic rotation slots. Node startup fails if bip152hb is configured alongside -blocksonly. Evidence of importance is limited to the author's description of operational requirements for low-latency and multi-datacenter topologies.
changed_since_previous: The configuration mechanism was redesigned from an opt-in `-addnode` suffix (`-addnode=<host>=bip152-hb`) to a new `bip152hb` flag in the net permissions system (`-whitelist` and `-whitebind`).
evidence: Author's PR description: 'For example, an operator may run nodes in multiple locations, or maintain a stable, low-latency link to another node, and want that peer to announce compact blocks immediately and consistently, including after reconnects, instead of waiting for automatic selection.'
problem: Node operators cannot force specific peers to relay compact blocks in high-bandwidth mode based on external topology knowledge. Bitcoin Core only selects up to three high-bandwidth peers dynamically based on who delivers new blocks first, meaning dedicated low-latency peering links or nodes operated across multiple datacenters must wait for dynamic selection and lose that state whenever connections reconnect.

risk.why: A mistake in compact block negotiation or peer bookkeeping in net_processing could cause redundant bandwidth consumption or protocol-level desynchronization in block announcements.

summary: Adds a `bip152hb` network permission flag configurable via `-whitelist` and `-whitebind`. When established, connections to peers with this permission immediately request BIP152 high-bandwidth compact block mode during the handshake. These peers operate outside of and in addition to the standard dynamic limit of three automatically selected high-bandwidth compact block peers.
